questions: Did slalom and s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 per run with wheel_track 0.10 m?
Does max_error at the first loss still reach 0.06 m, or has it fallen below it?
Does steering_oscillation go above the 0.23 to 0.27 seen at 0.12 m track, which would suggest the sharper turn is overcorrecting?
Did rms_error on the oval stay near 0.036, or did it change with the narrower track?
Is completion_time or base speed now the limit on progress, and is any run close to the 3 s limit?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: Report the step and bend of the first remaining line loss, and say whether the robot's response there looks too slow (drivetrain) or whether the tape is leaving the sensors (span). If oscillation has risen above 0.3 with losses still present, say whether the centroid or the turn response is the cause.

intent: Change one variable: wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m, with the 10 cm sensor span kept. I expect this to give sharper turning on the slalom and s-bend, cutting the remaining single line-loss event per run and bringing max_error below 0.06 m on tight bends. Sensor geometry and drivetrain otherwise stay fixed, so the race isolates the drivetrain effect.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that the 10 cm span removed most losses on the oval (0.05 per run) but not on the slalom (1.0 per run at max_error 0.0615 m). Sensor span is therefore not the sole limit. The drivetrain (wheel_track) is the next variable, as the Integrator's pre-agreed branch specified. Steering oscillation rose above the earlier range, so if oscillation is the problem after this change, the footprint or the centroid spacing is the next lever.
rationale: Iteration 2 (10 cm span, outer sensors at ±0.05 m) changed the failure pattern but did not end it. Line losses fell to 0.05 per run on oval, but stayed at 1.0 on slalom and 0.9 on s-bend, and every trial still ended off track with max_error about 0.061 to 0.064 m. Progress rose to 0.27 on s-bend and 0.51 on oval, and the score rose from 54.8 to 124.6. Sensor span from 6 cm to 10 cm therefore helped on the oval but is not the limit on the slalom, where the single excursion persists at the same max_error. Under the Integrator's pre-agreed branch, a persistent loss at about 0.06 m with span widened is the signal to change the drivetrain. I make that single change: wheel_track 0.12 m to 0.10 m, which gives sharper turn authority. Steering oscillation rose to 0.23 to 0.27 on oval and s-bend, above the earlier 0.08 to 0.16 range, so I am not also changing the footprint now. Changing two variables at once would make it impossible to tell which one caused the result. I keep the 10 cm span, footprints, body, mass and wheel radius unchanged. Expected result: slalom and s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 per run, and max_error on tight bends drops below 0.06 m. If oscillation rises further or losses persist, the next test is the 16 mm footprint for smoothing.
